description: Small, fixed, hand-curated retrieval benchmark dataset for M4 model-independent embedding evaluation.

documents.content: The agent runtime uses explicit states such as READY, RUNNING, WAITING_APPROVAL, and FAILED so transitions are deterministic and debuggable.
Each agent turn stores an immutable log of model output, selected tools, and execution outcomes for auditability.
Tools marked high risk require human approval before runtime execution, even if the model requests them.
The model gateway normalizes provider-specific outputs into typed messages and structured tool-call proposals.
Transient model transport failures can be retried by gateway policy, but invalid structured output is rejected instead of silently repaired.
A tool registry maps each unique tool name to its input schema, policy settings, and deterministic executor.
Tool input is schema-validated before side effects, ensuring malformed arguments cannot trigger execution.
Tool execution returns structured results with explicit success or failure outcomes and machine-readable error details.
EmbeddingProvider separates embedding generation from storage so retrievers and vector stores stay provider-independent.
LocalEmbeddingProvider may apply distinct query and document prefixes to support models that use instruction-tuned embedding prompts.
Vector-store collections must isolate embedding spaces by model identity and dimensionality so incompatible vectors never mix.
QdrantVectorStore supports provider-independent metadata filtering with exact-match predicates combined using logical AND.
Retriever behavior is: embed the natural-language query, then call vector_store.search with top_k and optional metadata filters.
M4 ingestion uses whole documents as the knowledge unit; automatic chunking is intentionally deferred to M5.
Execution tracing records tool name, validated arguments, duration_ms, and outcome to make deterministic flows observable.
A request identifier can link model calls, tool runs, and retrieval events into a single correlated execution timeline.
The retrieval benchmark dataset is manually curated and version-controlled so relevance judgments remain explicit and stable over time.
M4 retrieval quality metrics include Recall@K, Mean Reciprocal Rank, and NDCG@K.
Every candidate embedding model must be evaluated against the same documents, queries, and relevance judgments for fair comparison.
Local-first architecture favors running embedding inference on local hardware when practical, while still allowing portable abstractions.
Provider independence means domain APIs must not leak Qdrant-specific payload or client types to callers.
Document metadata can represent source, domain, or tags, but metadata filtering is complementary to semantic similarity rather than a replacement.
A playlist utility can sort tracks alphabetically by artist name for deterministic UI ordering.
A SQL diagnostics tool supports exact-match filtering on log severity and source service fields.
Benchmark queries should use natural paraphrases and user-style language, not only class names or exact implementation tokens.
The model may suggest actions, but policy-checked runtime logic is solely responsible for executing external side effects.
Qdrant and Ollama integration tests are opt-in and excluded from the default CI test path to keep routine checks lightweight.
Local validation commonly includes pytest, ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy, and pre-commit run --all-files.
Retrieval requests should reject empty query text and non-positive top_k values as configuration errors.
The initial M4 benchmark excludes chunking, reranking, and hybrid retrieval so the experiment stays narrow and reproducible.
